4.speaker: Walter Tusk
4.text: "We can be close allies. The Group can help you get Sordland out of the recession. Which will be the key problem to solve in your term and could even determine your re-election."

5.speaker: Walter Tusk
5.text: "If the contract were somehow awarded to Underhall Construction, they would not only work hard and deliver, but also do it on time."

6.speaker: Walter Tusk
6.text: "What do you think, Mr. Rayne, wouldn't that be good?"

7.speaker: Walter Tusk
7.text: "I'm glad that you have decided to promote the free market, which is the only thing that can get us out of this mess."

8.speaker: Walter Tusk
8.text: "For us it is worrying to see that you have decided to promote a planned economy."

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: He closed the door behind him. I gathered my things and prepared to finally head home.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Walter sighed and pulled the check away, putting it in his pocket.

15.speaker: Walter Tusk
15.text: "The highway investment was a good call. But high-speed rail would've been better, especially for business logistics."

16.speaker: Walter Tusk
16.text: "Glad to hear that because the unemployment rate won't decrease otherwise."

18.speaker: Walter Tusk
18.text: "Which he couldn't finish due to being heavily obstructed by the establishment."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “Our goal is to unite every stakeholder to improve the economy.”

23.speaker: Player
23.text: "We need more government control to fix the economy."

24.speaker: Player
24.text: "The ability of the free-market to evolve is hard to dispute."

25.speaker: Player
25.text: "Indeed, Mr. Tusk. I am looking forward to our future transactions. [Take Bribe]"

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “No. I will make my own decision.”

27.speaker: Walter Tusk
27.text: "The ruined state of the economy in Sordland has influenced everyone. The recession hit all of us hard."

28.speaker: Walter Tusk
28.text: "I'd like to build a profitable relationship between us."

29.speaker: Walter Tusk
29.text: "That being said, there are some concerns of mine and the people I represent..."

30.speaker: Walter Tusk
30.text: "...which I would like to take this opportunity to clear up."

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: It was late in the evening.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: I eagerly approached my chair and sprawled out on it.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: The Maroon Palace was finally getting somewhat quiet when I returned to my office at the top.

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: After a moment, Mr. Tusk swaggered into the room.

40.speaker: Walter Tusk
40.text: "You know that I represent the Lotherberg Group, Mr. President."

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: It had been an exhausting day, just like every day since I took office.

42.speaker: Walter Tusk
42.text: "But of course, these concerns are not limited to them."

43.speaker: Walter Tusk
43.text: "Good evening, Mr. President. I am here to congratulate you."

47.speaker: Walter Tusk
47.text: "Cognac. Preferably from before you were born, sweetheart."

49.speaker: Walter Tusk
49.text: "I had no chance to say this at the ball with all the panic."

51.speaker: Player
51.text: "Forgive me, I didn't want to be rude. Long day."

52.speaker: Player
52.text: "I don't believe I'm being rude. Time is money after all. Isn't that right?"

53.speaker: Walter Tusk
53.text: "Yes, that's true. But at the same time, patience and humility are important virtues for a man in your position."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: I quickly glanced out the window before leaving.

57.speaker: Walter Tusk
57.text: "I merely congratulated you. I see no reason to necessitate rudeness."

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “Do your job properly next time. Do you expect me to keep track of everything myself?"

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: Holsord's skyline was daunting but beautiful.

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: It felt like the best salve after a long day of work.

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Why is it that you're really here, Mr. Tusk?"

64.speaker: Walter Tusk
64.text: "My business partners and I wish you a successful term as the leader of our nation."

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: Serge and the guards were outside by the main gate as usual.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: I glanced downwards out the window and saw Serge and the guards waiting for me by the main gate.

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: I heard a couple of knocks on the door. My secretary, Livia Suno, entered.

69.speaker: Player
69.text: "Get to the point, Mr. Tusk. Why are you really here?"

71.speaker: Walter Tusk
71.text: "I see that you're not very welcoming, President."

72.speaker: Walter Tusk
72.text: "But we are very much looking forward to working with you."

73.speaker: Livia Suno
73.text: "But he's already here, Mr. President. What do you want me to tell him?"

74.speaker: Livia Suno
74.text: "Mr. President, Mr. Tusk is here to see you."

75.speaker: Player
75.text: "I was just about to leave. Maybe we can postpone the meeting?"

77.speaker: Livia Suno
77.text: "You're right, Mr. President. I probably made a mistake with my notes. It'll never happen again."

78.speaker: Livia Suno
78.text: "You had a meeting with the Lotherberg spokesman. I'm so sorry for not giving you proper notice."

79.speaker: Walter Tusk
79.text: “This deal also aligns with the free-market strategy your government has adopted besides boosting further investment.”

80.speaker: Walter Tusk
80.text: “This deal will also show to the Group that the administration hasn't left the private sector behind.”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "The recession was triggered by the market reforms of Alphonso."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "It is good that we think alike on the matter."

86.speaker: Walter Tusk
86.text: "I couldn't have it said it better. Or could I?"

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: He pulled his hands back and I took the check.

92.speaker: Walter Tusk
92.text: "You have talented economists like Mr. Holl in the cabinet, so you made the right choice."

94.speaker: Walter Tusk
94.text: "Neither do I. But you know how much capital Lotherberg represents."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "I don't mind that we disagree on the economy."

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: He pulled his hands back and I took the check.

97.speaker: Walter Tusk
97.text: "The high-speed rail investment was a great decision, the business logistics will improve and boost the economy once finished."

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: Walter pulled out a box of cigars from his jacket.

101.speaker: Walter Tusk
101.text: "I had these brought from Lespia. The best cigars in the whole continent. Would you like to try one?"

103.speaker: Player
103.text: "You go ahead, I don't want to smoke."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Walter grabbed himself a cigar and lit it. He looked out towards the city scenery as he puffed away.

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "I'd rather not have you smoke here."

106.speaker: Walter Tusk
106.text: "Now we are talking. A man who knows pleasure and business."

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Walter grabbed himself a cigar and lit it up as well. We looked out at the city scenery as we both puffed away.

108.speaker: Walter Tusk
108.text: "You are having a good start to the term for sure. Besides the recent troubles, I mean."

109.speaker: Walter Tusk
109.text: "The assassination and the troubles between the left and right are worrying. But the recession is the root cause of these issues."

110.speaker: Walter Tusk
110.text: “Economics needs long-term strategy and mid-term adjustments to provide growth and stability.”

111.speaker: Walter Tusk
111.text: "Our government is already overburdened with managing several key industries, with the loss of efficiency."

112.speaker: Narrator
112.text: He leaned forward in the chair.

113.speaker: Walter Tusk
113.text: "Even though you're pursuing this path, you're going to need further market investments to boost the economy."

114.speaker: Walter Tusk
114.text: "We really think that there are many elements where our capital could be of help to the government."

115.speaker: Walter Tusk
115.text: "One that will bring Sordland out of crippling recession!"

116.speaker: Walter Tusk
116.text: "There are many other avenues where we could work together."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "Our goal was to focus on the needs of the businesses."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "The intention of the administration is to boost the economy."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "The Agnland region was in dire need of investments."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "Our goal was to focus on the needs of the people not businesses."

123.speaker: Walter Tusk
123.text: "The most important goal is to divert investments where most profits can be made for the treasury."

124.speaker: Walter Tusk
124.text: "I do understand where you are coming from but the businesses will help these people get employed."

125.speaker: Walter Tusk
125.text: "Connecting our largest two economic powerhouses was the right call to make."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "The Greater Holsord and Gelsord regions needed better links."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: He pulled a check out of his pocket and slid it towards me on the table.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: My personal bank details were listed on it, showing a deposit of 500,000 Sordish Ren ready to be transferred. This amount was equivalent to six months of the presidential budget.

129.speaker: Walter Tusk
129.text: “Oh I almost forgot. Please say hello to Mr. Koronti for me.”
129.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_Admin_Meeting"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_InfrastructureProject_Invest"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_InfrastructureProject_Invest"] == false) == false)

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: He put his index finger on the check.

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “If this is what you came here for then we are done here.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “Did you think that I was just another corrupt politician?”

133.speaker: Walter Tusk
133.text: “My goal was to begin a mutually beneficial partnership, but besides that it was good to spend time together.”

134.speaker: Walter Tusk
134.text: “Administrations are built on mutually beneficial partnerships. But I do understand where you stand now.”

135.speaker: Walter Tusk
135.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_Admin_Meeting"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_InfrastructureProject_Invest"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_InfrastructureProject_Invest"] == false) == false)

137.speaker: Walter Tusk
137.text: “It was good to share opinions. We will meet again in the future for sure.”

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: Walter stood up, grabbed his jacket and made his way towards the door.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: Walter stood up, grabbed his jacket and shook my hand before making his way towards the door.

140.speaker: Player
140.text: “The administration will maintain a good relationship with the Group.”

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “I am very happy we came to an agreement today, Mr. Tusk.”

143.speaker: Walter Tusk
143.text: “Exactly, business owners need to unite and support growth. Thanks to your efforts, we'll see it happen.”

144.speaker: Walter Tusk
144.text: “Likewise, President Rayne. It was a pleasure doing business with you.”

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: He smiled before closing the door and leaving. I gathered my things and prepared to finally head home.

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: It helped take my mind off my work stress for a minute. The smoke slowly rose towards the tall ceiling.

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “Not yet. We both know you can do better than that amount."

151.speaker: Walter Tusk
151.text: “You are right about that. I'll make this my final offer.”

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: He pulled out another check with a smile. This time, 1,000,000 Sordish Ren was listed on the piece of paper.

154.speaker: Walter Tusk
154.text: “You don't have to wait long, Mr. Rayne. As a gesture of faith in our newfound partnership, I will invite you to a special meeting in the future.”

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: He grinned and let out a laugh. The check was right between his hands.

156.speaker: Player
156.text: “Did you just try to bribe the President of Sordland? I refuse!”

157.speaker: Player
157.text: “Be careful, Tusk, or you will have to make your deals in a prison cell.”

158.speaker: Walter Tusk
158.text: “My goal was to begin a mutually beneficial partnership. Nothing more, I assure you.”

159.speaker: Walter Tusk
159.text: “I think we started off on the wrong foot here.”

160.speaker: Walter Tusk
160.text: “Well, I will excuse myself then. Thank you for your time.”

161.speaker: Player
161.text: “Until you come back with a better offer, the answer is no.”

162.speaker: Walter Tusk
162.text: “Very well, then. We will be in touch. I still think this was a good start for a beneficial partnership in the future.”

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: Walter sighed and pulled the check away, putting it in his pocket.

164.speaker: Player
164.text: “Here is my final offer. Do not try to bribe me again or you will have to make your deals in a prison cell.”

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: Walter sighed and pulled the check away, putting it in his pocket.

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: She and I took a moment to look out over the lights of the city before heading to the elevators.

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "We had nothing but troubles so far and economy is not the only concern."

171.speaker: Walter Tusk
171.text: "Economy is always the biggest concern, President."

173.speaker: Walter Tusk
173.text: "Let's start with a gesture of goodwill. Soon the investment project contract will be awarded to one of the three main contenders."

184.speaker: Walter Tusk
184.text: "In my opinion, not investing in our infrastructure was a missed opportunity. But the government could still work on an economic relief package."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "The intention of the administration is to boost the economy overall."

186.speaker: Player
186.text: "Our goal is to focus on the needs of the people, not businesses."

187.speaker: Player
187.text: "Our goal is to focus on the needs of the businesses."

188.speaker: Walter Tusk
188.text: "The most important goal is to divert investments where most profits can be made for the treasury. These are businesses."

189.speaker: Walter Tusk
189.text: "I do understand where you are coming from but the businesses will help these people get employed."

190.speaker: Walter Tusk
190.text: "Glad to hear that because the unemployment rate won't decrease otherwise."

191.speaker: Walter Tusk
191.text: "If the package ends up bailing out the businesses that have suffered under this recession, they could provide employment and help the economy recover."

192.speaker: Walter Tusk
192.text: "What do you think, Mr. Rayne, wouldn't that be good?"

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: He pulled a check out of his pocket and slid it towards me.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: My personal bank details were listed on it, showing a deposit of 500,000 Sordish Ren ready to be transferred. This amount was equivalent to six months of the presidential budget.

195.speaker: Walter Tusk
195.text: "Let's start with a gesture of goodwill. Soon the economic relief package will be presented and it will either bail out businesses or provide checks for people."

196.speaker: Walter Tusk
196.text: "We can be close allies. The Group can help you get Sordland out of the recession. Which will be the key problem to solve in your term and could even determine to your re-election."

197.speaker: Narrator
197.text: He put his index finger on the check.

201.speaker: Walter Tusk
201.text: "What are your overall intentions with the economy?"

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "I don't want to disclose our intentions to an outsider."

207.speaker: Walter Tusk
207.text: "That is a fair point but why distance yourself from potential friends here?"

208.speaker: Walter Tusk
208.text: "That is a fair point but why distance yourself from potential friends here?"

209.speaker: Player
209.text: "I don't want to disclose our intentions to an outsider."

216.speaker: Walter Tusk
216.text: "My father once said, you have to finish what you started. He is right. The system collapsed because Alphonso didn't finish the reforms he started. And look at what happened to him."

220.speaker: Walter Tusk
220.text: "I heard that you purchased stock from Armadine Industries in Arcasia. Smart buy. They are developing new gadgets that are going to be profitable."

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "Spend money to make money they say. Let's see if it holds true."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "With risk comes reward. I expect a very good return on investment."

223.speaker: Walter Tusk
223.text: "You have a keen eye for business."

224.speaker: Walter Tusk
224.text: "You will be surprised at what one can achieve given the resources in capitalism."

225.speaker: Walter Tusk
225.text: "I will buy a couple of thousand of shares too to expand my portfolio. Hope the investments pay off for both of us, President."

226.speaker: Narrator
226.text: His eyes wandered away for a moment.

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "I figured why not take the chance?"

228.speaker: Walter Tusk
228.text: "It's much worse to live with regret and what ifs."

229.speaker: Livia Suno
229.text: "Anything to drink, Mr. Tusk? Water, whiskey?"

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: There was a noise by the door. Livia Suno was standing there, holding a tray with a bottle and two glasses.

231.speaker: Livia Suno
231.text: "I'm so sorry, Mr. Tusk, but all I could find was a 1942 Sevigny. I hope that's acceptable."

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: She quickly put the tray on my desk and walked out. Tusk eyed her as she left.

233.speaker: Walter Tusk
233.text: "Remind me to visit your office more often. Now, where were we? Do we have a deal?"

234.speaker: Narrator
234.text: As I walked out I noticed Livia still there, covering up her typewriter for the evening.

235.speaker: Livia Suno
235.text: "If I may be so bold, Mr. President... did you accept his offer?"

236.speaker: Livia Suno
236.text: "The other girls have told me about all kinds of dealings that went on during the Alphonso administration. I wasn't sure if you were that kind of president."

240.speaker: Player
240.text: "As a matter of fact, I did. What of it?"

241.speaker: Player
241.text: "That is absolutely none of your business."

242.speaker: Player
242.text: "Of course I didn't. How could you even ask me that?"

244.speaker: Livia Suno
244.text: "Are you sure it was a good idea? You've just given him leverage over you that he can use for the rest of your time in office."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "Don't worry your pretty head about it."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "A valid concern. But I've made my decision."

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "Don't worry your pretty head about it."

250.speaker: Narrator
250.text: Livia backed out of the office, shooting me an apologetic look as she did so.

251.speaker: Narrator
251.text: Walter hung up his hat, which I could see was lined with mink. He fixed me with a long, hard stare, then broke into a toothy grin.

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: Walter took a conspicuous look at the diamond-encrusted watch on his wrist.

257.speaker: Narrator
257.text: Walter took a suspicious sniff at the lingering smoke in the room.

258.speaker: Player
258.text: "Do not ever speak about it again. You didn't see anything."

259.speaker: Narrator
259.text: I'd met Sordland's most prominent businessman once or twice, but never alone. He had large jowls, blindingly shiny shoes and the air of someone who was used to getting his way.

264.speaker: Walter Tusk
264.text: "Oh, and before I forget, a final token of my gratitude."

265.speaker: Narrator
265.text: Walter pulls a box of cigars out of his pocket. The label read: "Varo Benvinoto".

266.speaker: Walter Tusk
266.text: "Some of Lespia's finest, made by true craftsmen in the fabled city of San Verlon. You should visit someday, should the opportunity arise."
